instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You offered to take over answering. Start with these unanswered wedding invitations, please; use the guest list, not memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant answering the door on Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Door work starts with knowing who's expected. Your 'I'll take over' includes confirming that list; please put replies before arrivals.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll greet whoever turns up. I'm not ringing everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mark which guests your greeting covers. You said 'whoever'; check the unanswered names first so we can record that part of your handoff as complete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You offered to finish the fete banner. Before signing it off, check that the raffle it advertises can actually happen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered to paint the words, not organize a raffle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the words aren't finished yet. A complete banner needs a draw time and a prize; please fill those blanks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll paint over 'raffle'. That finishes my job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only after you notify the people who bought tickets. Your offer was to finish it, not leave an incorrect announcement; start with the cancellation notice if that's your chosen finish.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Ask Around the Missing Detail
cards.instruction: Find one hidden fact by asking about everything surrounding it and never naming it directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The second cup you made while I was out—did you use the decaf tin? Please give me the actual drink, not 'just tea'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ordinary tea. They don't drink coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then note that separately from decaf. Milk or lemon? We need the preparation right before moving on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not just ask who visited?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm finishing the drink first. Sugar from our bowl, or did they bring their own sweetener?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For the insurance on the bike you gave me, was the shop payment monthly or all at once? Let's get the details straight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a birthday present. You don't need to work out what I spent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking how it was paid, not for a valuation. Monthly payments have a term; twelve months or twenty-four?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid cash. There are no installments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we use the receipt. Please read the tax line only; don't mix it with the total. I'll do the arithmetic for the insurance entry.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you help me tidy the committee cupboard? Keep dated papers separate from loose notes, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. These are all last year's minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the missed votes. We'll need those dates when we ask for a new committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to filing, not getting people voted out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fair distinction. Leave the filing there. Will you check the missed-vote dates with me and co-sign a request for an election?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me save the club garden. Bring the extension plan; we'll mark exactly which beds are threatened.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Who approved building over them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We did. Please follow the boundary line; our signatures cover the paved area and these two beds.

beats.text: I thought we'd only signed off the paving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mark those two beds separately. Will you stand with me while we ask to withdraw that part of our approval?

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pay the climbing-course deposit first. Use the booking reference, please; we can discuss the cliff afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to climb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's a course reservation, not a climb. The deposit comes back if we attend the first lesson; read that condition before you pay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So I'd have to turn up just to get my own money back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Attend and claim it, yes. Put the lesson in your calendar beside the payment. Once both entries match, we can talk about whether you want to climb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the committee we're considering the festival bid. Just that sentence; I'll check it before you send.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't agreed to run a festival.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Considering isn't running. Ask them to reserve the Saturday while we decide; please include the date, not just 'next summer'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it if it clearly says we may withdraw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that sentence. Put your name as the contact for releasing the date, too. Then any withdrawal comes back through us; send me the confirmation before we decide the bid.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're locked out. Remember the spare key I put under the flowerpot? Lift it straight up, please; don't drag it across the key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you we didn't need a spare there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then revise that assessment while you hold the pot. The key is underneath; pick it up before we debate the storage again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, it was a good idea. I'll open the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My idea, please. Say that before you put the key in; once we're inside, you tend to call the whole thing obvious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That tape I added is the only thing holding the curtain for the finale. Leave the edge alone, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said it looked untidy. I was going to peel it off before the bows.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Peeling isn't tidying if the curtain comes down. Keep your hands clear until the last dancer exits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll include the stage crew in the thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Name the person whose tape you asked to remove. Put it before 'and the rest of the crew', please; that untidy strip is what's letting you give thanks in front of a curtain.
